items.markdown:
If you’re looking around Leicester, there are currently blue Staffy listings in the wider Leicestershire/Midlands area. I’d treat adverts as leads rather than endorsements and prioritise the breeder’s health testing and welfare practices.

### Places to look

- **Royal Kennel Club — Find a Puppy:** This is the first place I’d check. Its Staffordshire Bull Terrier search lets you filter for puppies whose parents have been health tested. [royalkennelclub.com](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/find-a-puppy/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **Staffie Owners:** Their Leicester/Leicestershire listings currently include blue Staffies, including adverts in the surrounding Midlands. [Staffie-Owners.co.uk](https://www.staffie-owners.co.uk/staffies-for-sale/leicester-leicestershire?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [Staffie-Owners.co.uk](https://www.staffie-owners.co.uk/staffies-for-sale/leicester-leicestershire?colour=blue&ready_to_leave=now&sex=male&utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- **Pets4Homes:** Current Leicester-area results include blue litters around Nuneaton, Birmingham and elsewhere in the Midlands, as well as breeders advertising KC registration and health testing. [Pets4Homes](https://www.pets4homes.co.uk/sale/puppies/staffordshire-bull-terrier/united-kingdom/england/leicester/leicester/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

A useful local point of contact is The Staffordshire Bull Terrier Club in Cannock. Breed clubs can be particularly useful for finding established breeders rather than simply searching adverts.

### What I'd ask the breeder

For a Staffy, **don't let the blue colour be the deciding factor**. Blue is an accepted Staffordshire Bull Terrier colour, but The Royal Kennel Club specifically advises putting health and temperament ahead of colour. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

Ask these questions:

1. **“Can I see the mother's health-test certificates and the father's?”**

 - HC-HSF4 hereditary cataracts
- L-2-HGA
- Eye examination, including PHPV/litter screening
- Elbow testing
- Patella testing
 These are among the tests/screening relevant to Staffies under current breed-health guidance. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/media/cvef530x/kc_health_standard_07-25-web.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
2. **“Can I see the actual certificates/results, rather than just being told they're health tested?”**
 You can independently check KC-recorded results through its health-results service.
3. **“Can I meet the puppy with its mum, where the puppies were raised?”**
 You should see the mother interacting naturally with the litter. Be cautious if you're offered a meeting somewhere other than the breeder's home.
4. **“How have the puppies been socialised?”**
 Ask specifically about children, household noises, handling, other dogs, car journeys and being left briefly alone.
5. **“Can I see the puppy's microchip, vaccination and worming records?”**
6. **“Are the puppies KC registered, and can I see the registration details and pedigree?”**
 KC registration isn't by itself proof of good breeding, so don't let registration substitute for health evidence.
7. **“How many litters does the mother have had, and how old is she?”**
8. **“What happens if my vet finds a significant health problem shortly after purchase?”**
 Ask to see the written puppy contract and health guarantee before paying a deposit.
9. **“What food are they eating, and can I take some home?”**
 A good breeder should be able to tell you exactly what the puppy has been eating.

### Red flags 🚩

Walk away if the breeder:

- won't let you see the puppy **with its mother**
- refuses to show original health-test results
- has numerous breeds/litters constantly available
- pressures you to pay a deposit immediately
- wants to meet in a car park or other neutral location
- says things like **“blue is rare, so it's automatically worth ££££”**
- has puppies that look lethargic, dirty, excessively fearful or unwell
- claims “KC registered” means the parents are health tested.

There are currently blue Staffy adverts around Leicester at roughly **£1,550–£2,500**, but price alone tells you very little about quality; current adverts show substantial variation in location, testing and breeder credentials. [Staffie-Owners.co.uk](https://www.staffie-owners.co.uk/staffies-for-sale/leicester-leicestershire?colour=blue&ready_to_leave=now&sex=male&utm_source=chatgpt.com) [Pets4Homes](https://www.pets4homes.co.uk/sale/puppies/staffordshire-bull-terrier/united-kingdom/england/leicester/leicester/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

If you tell me **how far you're willing to travel from Leicester (e.g. 25, 50 or 75 miles)** and whether you want a **male or female**, I can search the current listings and narrow them down based on **health testing, breeder licensing and distance**, rather than simply picking the cheapest puppy.
